From research

The projects behind my work on perception, mapping, and near-ground aerial autonomy.

At Fraunhofer IVI, I work in collaborative research projects that connect algorithms with sensors, robotic systems, and field demonstrations. Here is a closer look at what each project sets out to do and my part in it.

01 / Perception / Reliability

VERUM.

Trustworthy perception for aerial autonomy.

Completed

2023 - 2025

About the project

VERUM developed an architecture for reliable environment perception in urban air mobility. It brought together AI, multimodal sensing, and semantic mapping to help aircraft understand their surroundings.

  • Trustworthy AI
  • Multimodal sensing
  • Semantic occupancy maps
Project overview ↗Open-source Radix ↗

My contribution

  • Curated aerial datasets and trained semantic and panoptic segmentation models.
  • Co-developed the live 3D voxel-mapping module, helping lay the foundation for online semantic map building.
  • Co-developed SSP to improve temporal consistency in aerial semantic segmentation.

Research outputs

SSP · CVPR 2025 ↗

02 / Sensor fusion / Collision avoidance

NiKoLaS.

Detecting obstacles that do not announce themselves.

Published term ended

Oct 2023 - Sep 2026

About the project

NiKoLaS investigates collision avoidance close to the ground, especially during takeoff and landing. Radar and infrared sensing help detect hazards such as cranes, vehicles, and people, including obstacles that do not transmit their position.

  • Radar + infrared
  • Obstacle detection
  • Near-ground flight
Official project page ↗

My contribution

  • Acquired and processed aerial datasets, and trained segmentation models for an infrared-only scene-parsing pipeline.
  • Integrated DAV3 metric depth estimation into the perception pipeline.
  • Provided perception outputs that are fused with dynamic obstacle detections in Max’s motion-forecasting module.

Motion forecasting: Maximilian Bialdyga

Special thanks to Paul, Tomaž, Andreas, and Vamsi for their great help.

NiKoLaS data collection, field setup, and flight trials.

03 / Semantic 3D mapping / Field demonstrations

ADAM.

High-definition maps for the lower airspace.

Final phase

Sep 2023 - Dec 2026

About the project

ADAM (Advanced Air Space Mapping) develops detailed, semantically annotated 3D maps for safer drone operations. It connects aerial data collection and mapping with localization, flight planning, and airspace services.

  • HD semantic 3D maps
  • Aerial data
  • Flight demonstrations
Official project page ↗Final presentation ↗

My contribution

  • Acquired, processed, and annotated aerial datasets, and trained segmentation models for offline and live 3D map building.
  • Co-developed MultiFly for efficient multimodal dataset creation through RGB-to-X label propagation across heterogeneous sensors.
  • Used VoxelFix to clean up semantic artifacts in the resulting 3D maps.
  • Presented our work on high-definition 3D semantic mapping, including map-based pre-flight checks of planned flight paths, and participated in the project’s demo flights.

Research outputs

MultiFly ↗VoxelFix ↗

ADAM final presentation and demonstration flights · October 2026

04 / Scene understanding / Assisted flight

ENGEL.

Helping rescue helicopters land in unfamiliar terrain.

Ongoing

LuFo VI-3 research project

About the project

ENGEL explores sensing and AI assistance for rescue helicopters. Better awareness of terrain and obstacles supports flight, approach, and landing, with the aim of making demanding missions safer and more efficient.

  • Environment perception
  • Sensor fusion
  • Landing assistance
Project overview ↗Consortium perspective ↗

My contribution

  • Developing semantic scene parsing and landing-spot detection for aerial environments.
  • Fusing static satellite-map information with live Radix maps to support downstream tasks.
  • Implementing on-board 3D map building and a map server for the perception and landing pipeline.
